chapter: Ch. 5 — From Workload to Model Selection (§5.3.2)
evidence: PDF p.134 (book p.110): "(Llama‑2 70B is not a GQA‑8 example: it uses 64 KV heads, so its per‑token KV matches the ~2.62 MB full‑MHA form above.)" — directly contradicts PDF p.169 (book p.145, Ch. 7 §7.3): "LLaMA-2 70B, for instance, has 64 query heads but only 8 KV-heads, so per-token KV shrinks by the head ratio to KVGQA per-token = 2 × 80 × (8 × 128) × 2 B ≈0.33 MB/token".
issue: Cross-chapter contradiction on a repeated model fact (KV-head count of Llama-2 70B), and the Ch. 5 version is also factually wrong: Meta's Llama-2-70B config (num_key_value_heads = 8) and the Llama 2 paper (GQA used in the 70B model) confirm 8 KV heads, giving ~0.33 MB/token at FP16 (~3.0 GB per 9.2K request), not the full-MHA ~2.62 MB/token (~24.1 GB). A reader sizing KV for Llama-2 70B from Ch. 5 would over-provision the KV cache 8× (or wrongly conclude the model cannot use the GQA constant that Ch. 7 and Table 5-2's own GQA-8 row apply to Llama-3 70B).
fix_instruction: Correct Ch. 5 §5.3.2's parenthetical to agree with Ch. 7 §7.3 and the Llama-2 70B config, e.g.: '(Llama-2 70B, like Llama-3 70B, is a GQA-8 example: 8 KV heads × 128 → ~0.33 MB/token at FP16; the ~2.62 MB/token full-MHA constant is the canonical teaching geometry, not a named 70B checkpoint).' Then sweep both chapters for any other Llama-2-70B KV statements to confirm only this one instance is wrong.

evidence: PDF p.153 (book p.129): "We see: p95 TTFT climbing (serving), KV cache hit ratio low (resource: FLOP/reuse — prefill recomputation), and prefill queue depth growing" — but the same chapter's mini-case (PDF p.157) reads "low prefix-hit ratio", §6.6 (PDF p.156) reads "Prefix-cache hit rates", and Ch. 2's vocabulary table (PDF p.44) explicitly separates "KV cache" ("not an optimization over a shared prefix") from "prefix caching / KV reuse" ("reusing already-computed K/V for a shared prefix, to skip re-prefilling it").
issue: Terminology drift on a repeated diagnostic metric: 'KV cache hit ratio' names the stored-state object, but the quantity meant (and glossed inline as 'FLOP/reuse — prefill recomputation') is the prefix-cache hit ratio. The book's own Ch. 2 vocabulary table and Preface ('load-bearing contrasts are never relaxed') require the two terms to stay distinct, yet Ch. 6 uses both names for the same counter within four pages.
fix_instruction: Replace 'KV cache hit ratio' in §6.3.4 with 'prefix-cache hit ratio' (the normative term per Ch. 2's vocabulary table, §6.6 and the §6.8 mini-case), then sweep Chapter 6 for any further instances of the 'KV cache hit' phrasing.
